name: The Best Apple Crisp

ingredients.name: freshly grated lemon zest, from 1 whole lemon
unsalted butter, cut into small cubes and chilled

instructions.primary_message: For the Topping: Adjust oven rack to middle position and preheat to 375°F. In a food processor, pulse flour, raw sugar, lemon zest, nutmeg, and salt until well combined, about 3 pulses. Add pecans; pulse just until pecans start to break apart, 2 to 3 pulses. (Some whole pecans should still be visible.) Add butter and pulse until mixture resembles a coarse meal, with pea-sized chunks, 20 to 25 pulses. Transfer to a large bowl and chill in refrigerator or freezer until ready to bake.

To Assemble and Bake: In a large mixing bowl, toss apples, sugar, cornstarch, salt, and whiskey until evenly coated. Transfer to a 2-quart baking dish; cover with crisp topping, spreading it into an even layer across the dish. Do not pack topping down with your hands. Bake until topping is golden brown, and apples are tender when pierced with a fork, about 45 minutes. Let crisp cool for at least 15 minutes before serving.

description: This apple crisp recipe has a crumbly, buttery topping and a filling with complex layers of flavor: soft fruit, lemon, nutmeg and caramel.
notes:
Optional substitutions: bourbon → rye or Scotch

Notes: You can substitute 1 teaspoon (4 blades) mace in place of the nutmeg for a more complex flavor.
We recommend using a mix of firm, tart apples like Fuji and Jonagold, as well as softer Golden Delicious.

Make-ahead and storage: The topping can be made up to 5 days in advance and refrigerated in an airtight container. The topping can be frozen for up to 3 months.
Leftover crisp can be stored in an airtight container for 3 to 4 days. Reheat in a 350ºF (175ºC) oven or microwave until warmed through.
Once cooled, the crisp can be wrapped tightly in foil and plastic wrap and rozen for up to 3 months.
author: Max Falkowitz
